**Finding: missing (insurance clause absent) — redline validated and submitted.**

What I checked:
- Full-text search for "insurance" — zero hits across the document.
- Read the entire general/miscellaneous block (Sections 13–30, p0078–p0097) and the section outline; there is no insurance covenant, and no Exhibit carries one (Exhibits A and B are pricing placeholders, both "to be agreed").
- Confirmed "Customer Data" is not a defined term here, so the inserted clause uses the document's own terminology ("Client Content and any other data of Client or its customers").

Why it matters directionally: TrueLink is the hosting vendor operating our web site and processing consumer mortgage and credit-repository data. Combined with a vendor liability cap of 12 months' hosting/support fees (p0077), uninsured vendor exposure sits in the rule's walk-away territory.

The fix: a new Section 31 inserted after Force Majeure at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, certificates on request. The fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) is offered in the comment as a landing zone.

One drafting point flagged in the rationale rather than as a separate deviation: the survival clause at p0090 reads "Sections 1 and 5 through 30," so it should be conformed to pick up the new Section 31 — worth catching in the next turn of the document, since the clause requires coverage for one year post-term.
